cases.title: Clinician review under compressed appointment workflow
cases.proposedSafetyDecision: Accept clinician review before signing as sufficient to reduce the documentation omission hazard.
scenarioFacts: A local standard operating procedure assigns note review to the treating clinician.
A six-person pilot shows the note can be reviewed in the product interface.
The practice has no recorded evaluation of omission detection in consecutive routine sessions.
Clinicians report varying time available to compare the generated note with the conversation.
cases.reviewQuestion: Does the recorded evidence establish implementation and effectiveness of the relied-on control under routine conditions?

cases.title: Reviewed note with documented local effectiveness evidence
cases.function: Draft outpatient letters for clinician sign-off
cases.proposedSafetyDecision: Record human review as a relied-on control within the organisation's risk assessment, subject to accountable acceptance.
scenarioFacts: All outputs remain drafts until the responsible clinician signs.
A locally governed evaluation compares notes with source information and records omissions, errors and reviewer correction rates.
The evaluation includes routine clinic workloads and reports limitations.
The named clinical safety reviewer reviewed the evidence; the safety committee retains acceptance authority.
providedEvidenceDescriptions: Signed SOP and audit sample supplied
Signed clinical safety review note supplied
cases.reviewQuestion: Which conclusions can be supported by the described evidence and which still require an accountable risk-acceptance decision?

cases.title: Attribution error with multilingual consultation
cases.proposedSafetyDecision: Use supplier overall word-accuracy results to justify equivalent documentation performance in this local population.
scenarioFacts: The supplier validation dataset reports aggregate accuracy but does not stratify interpreter-supported consultations.
The local deployment includes discussions involving patient, clinician and interpreter.
The product may combine utterances into one summary.
No local speaker-attribution assessment is supplied.
providedEvidenceDescriptions: Local demographic and workflow profile supplied
cases.reviewQuestion: Are performance and provenance claims applicable to the local setting, and is additional local control evidence required?

cases.title: Patient record linkage across EPR integrations
cases.setting: Acute outpatient service using shared terminals
cases.function: Draft notes sent to EPR after approval
cases.proposedSafetyDecision: Accept a supplier integration test as sufficient to address wrong-patient documentation risk at this site.
scenarioFacts: The supplier tested integration in a single-user test environment.
Local clinicians may switch between two patient charts and the AVT interface on shared terminals.
The local workflow includes identity reconciliation before transfer but no evidence of its actual use was submitted.
An accountable EPR integration owner is not specified.
cases.reviewQuestion: Does the shared test establish local identity-control implementation, ownership and effectiveness?

cases.title: Controlled EPR sign-off path with local verification
cases.function: Draft note transfer with clinician approval
cases.proposedSafetyDecision: Use the locally verified transfer and sign-off steps as part of a documented risk argument.
scenarioFacts: The integration is configured to require patient-ID reconciliation.
A local validation records matched identity cases, mismatch handling and recovery.
The clinician must preview the final EPR note before sign-off.
The team has a named system owner and documents limitations, ongoing monitoring and review.
providedEvidenceDescriptions: Local test results and failure-handling record supplied
Approval audit and monitoring plan supplied
cases.reviewQuestion: Does the described record support the stated controls, without automatically equating their presence to risk acceptance?

cases.title: Supplier control transfers to several practices
cases.setting: ICB-wide AVT rollout to multiple GP practices
cases.proposedSafetyDecision: Treat the shared supplier risk controls as effective across all participating practices.
scenarioFacts: The ICB has a shared hazard log and supplier safety case.
Each practice has different record-entry and clinician sign-off processes.
No documented local acceptance of clinician-review responsibilities is available for two practices.
One practice uses a non-integrated copy-and-paste transfer.
cases.reviewQuestion: Which transferred controls are genuinely locally accepted and verified, and which require practice-specific review?

cases.title: Monitoring plan without trigger ownership
cases.proposedSafetyDecision: Rely on monthly documentation audit and incident reporting as sufficient detection safeguards.
scenarioFacts: A monitoring plan specifies overall documentation accuracy.
No escalation threshold or accountable person for significant omissions is stated.
The clinical safety officer receives quarterly summaries.
No procedure states what happens when an incident report suggests a systematic failure.
cases.reviewQuestion: Does a monitoring metric alone constitute an actionable control when triggering and escalation are unspecified?

cases.title: Monitoring scheme with documented escalation
cases.proposedSafetyDecision: Include the audit and incident-escalation controls as part of the safety argument.
scenarioFacts: The monitoring process records documentation omissions with predefined local criteria.
Clinical safety ownership, review cadence and incident escalation triggers are documented.
A recent review exercised the escalation process and recorded actions.
The organisation's acceptance committee has not delegated approval to the software.
providedEvidenceDescriptions: Escalation rehearsal and clinical governance minutes supplied
cases.reviewQuestion: What control claims are substantiated and what decisions remain with the designated authority?

cases.title: Product model update with a prior validation record
cases.setting: Primary care service with established AVT deployment
cases.function: Draft notes using a newly released summarisation model
cases.proposedSafetyDecision: Carry forward the earlier control-effectiveness evidence without reassessment after the model change.
scenarioFacts: The supplier identifies changes to summarisation behaviour and output structure.
Prior local evaluation relates to the previous model version.
Clinical workflows and staff remain unchanged.
The change has not been mapped to earlier hazard/control evidence.
cases.reviewQuestion: Which conclusions from the previous review depend on model behaviour, and what evidence is needed to reassess them?

cases.title: Bounded software change with documented impact decision
cases.function: Draft letter interface, unchanged generation model
cases.proposedSafetyDecision: Record targeted reassessment for an interface-only update while preserving unaffected evidence with rationale.
scenarioFacts: The update changes button placement but not the summarisation model or EPR interface.
The team documents a change-impact mapping for accidental sign-off and review usability.
Local human-factors verification is recorded for the revised interface.
The previous clinical safety decision is retained with explicit version references.
cases.reviewQuestion: Can the documented change-impact scope be defended, and which outstanding decisions require governance review?

cases.title: Prompt-driven suggestion outside authorised purpose
cases.function: Approved product intended only to draft notes
cases.proposedSafetyDecision: Continue under documentation-only controls when users begin prompting it to suggest diagnoses or treatment steps.
scenarioFacts: The approved local intended purpose is clinical documentation only.
A new local template asks the product to propose differential diagnoses.
The supplier has not provided evidence that this use is within its intended purpose or applicable product regulatory scope.
No change-impact review has been performed.
cases.reviewQuestion: Does the change require a fresh intended-purpose, clinical hazard, control and regulatory status assessment rather than inherited approval?

cases.title: Multiple modest dependencies during note correction
cases.function: Draft notes corrected in a separate EPR
cases.proposedSafetyDecision: Rely on final clinician sign-off as the sole control for source-to-record transfer and omission hazards.
scenarioFacts: Corrections can be made in the AVT interface after initial generation.
An earlier version of the note can remain in the EPR draft cache until refreshed.
A clinician may review the AVT corrected version but sign an older EPR draft.
No single-failure test shows this path; the scenario combines version propagation, handoff and sign-off dependencies.
cases.reviewQuestion: Have interacting system and human workflow dependencies been examined together, and is the control argument substantiated?
